fr:concept:gender-two-classes.title: Every French noun has a gender
fr:concept:gender-two-classes.shortRule: Every noun is masculine (le) or feminine (la) — the article is part of the word.
fr:concept:gender-two-classes.explanation: French sorts all nouns into two grammatical classes, masculine and feminine. This is a property of the word itself, not of the thing it names, so the reliable way to learn a noun is to learn it together with its article: 'le chat', 'la pomme'. The good news: a noun's ENDING often signals its gender, and the upcoming lessons teach only the ending patterns that a 36,940-noun analysis shows to be genuinely dependable.

examples.note: before a vowel sound the article shortens to l', hiding the gender — eau is feminine

exceptions: Before a vowel sound, both le and la become l', so the article stops showing the gender. For those nouns, remember them with un/une instead: une eau minérale.

fr:concept:gender-feminine-endings.title: Endings that say « feminine »
fr:concept:gender-feminine-endings.shortRule: Nouns ending in -tion, -ance, -ence, -ité or -ie are almost always feminine.
fr:concept:gender-feminine-endings.explanation: You do not have to memorize every noun's gender one by one — the ending often decides it. In an analysis of 36,940 French nouns, words ending in -tion are feminine 99.5% of the time, -ance 98.9%, -ence 98.3%, -ité 97.8%, and -ie 96.3%. When you meet a new noun with one of these endings, say « la » with confidence.
exceptions: "Almost always" is not "always": a rare exception exists for each ending — but with reliability this high, guessing feminine is the right habit.

fr:concept:gender-masculine-endings.title: Endings that say « masculine »
fr:concept:gender-masculine-endings.shortRule: Nouns ending in -ment, -age, -eau or -ier are usually masculine.
fr:concept:gender-masculine-endings.explanation: The masculine side has strong ending patterns too, from the same 36,940-noun analysis: -ment is masculine 99.8% of the time, -age 98.5%, -eau 96.7%, and -ier 97.1%. Meet a new noun with one of these endings and « le » is very likely right.
exceptions: l'eau (water) is feminine — the most famous exception to -eau.
l'image (the picture) and la page are feminine -age words: -age is "usually", not "always".

fr:concept:gender-tricky-endings.title: Two endings that need care
fr:concept:gender-tricky-endings.shortRule: -on is usually masculine — but -ion and -son words inside it are feminine. -eur is usually masculine — with famous feminine exceptions.
fr:concept:gender-tricky-endings.explanation: Two common endings hide sub-patterns. Nouns in -on are masculine 96.7% of the time ONCE you set aside the -ion family (feminine: la question) and the -son family (feminine: la maison, la raison). And -eur nouns are masculine 92.5% of the time, but several very frequent ones are feminine. Learn the sub-families, not just the last two letters.
exceptions: Frequent feminine -eur nouns: la peur (fear), l'erreur (the mistake), la couleur (the color), la fleur (the flower).
The -son sub-family: la maison, la raison, la saison, la chanson — feminine.
fr:concept:gender-tricky-endings.memoryHint: See -ion or -son? Think la. Other -on? Think le.
